record.paper_title: Tensegrity frameworks: Dynamic analysis review and open problems
record.original_question: For tensegrity structures whose desired set point or path has already been chosen by form finding, static design, or dynamic path planning, what passive or active control techniques can compensate for inaccuracies or absence of a dynamic model and for unknown external perturbations, so that the structure does not oscillate when it should remain still and can follow the desired path?

evidence.page: ScienceDirect HTML section: Control of tensegrity structures
evidence.quote: The main issues regarding the control of tensegrity structures are associated to its dynamic model.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tensegrity structure is a prestressed pin-jointed framework consisting of a finite set of rigid bars (struts) in compression and a set of elastic cables in tension, in static equilibrium under the internal self-stress. Denote by q(t) ∈ R^n the vector of nodal coordinates (configuration) of such a structure and by its dynamics the (generally nonlinear, possibly nonsmooth due to cable slackening) equations of motion of the form M(q) q̈ + C(q, q̇) q̇ + g(q) = B(q) u + w(t), where u ∈ R^m collects the control inputs (for example, rest-length actuations of selected cables or forces applied at selected nodes), w(t) is an unknown bounded external perturbation, and M, C, g, B are only partially known. Suppose that a desired equilibrium configuration q* (chosen by form finding or static design) or a desired feasible trajectory q*(t) (chosen by dynamic path planning) has been prescribed.

Design a passive control law (a choice of mechanical damping elements and prestress) and/or an active feedback control law u = K(q, q̇, t) with the following properties simultaneously:
(i) Robustness to model uncertainty: the closed-loop tracking error e(t) = q(t) − q*(t) (or e(t) = q(t) − q* in the regulation case) remains uniformly bounded and converges to a neighborhood of zero whose size can be made arbitrarily small, despite inaccurate or absent knowledge of M, C, g, B.
(ii) Disturbance rejection: the same property holds in the presence of unknown but bounded perturbations w(t).
(iii) Vibration suppression at rest: when q* is a constant set point, the closed-loop response exhibits no sustained oscillations, i.e., q̇(t) → 0 asymptotically.
(iv) Admissibility: the control respects the unilateral constraint that cables can only transmit tension (no compression), and the prestress remains within feasible bounds throughout the motion.

Provide such a control design, together with a proof of its stability and performance guarantees, for general tensegrity structures.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction in the dynamic analysis of tensegrity structures. While various partial control schemes (PID, LQR, sliding mode, adaptive, and passivity-based controllers) have been proposed in the literature for specific tensegrity classes, no general control technique is known that simultaneously handles arbitrary model inaccuracies, unknown bounded perturbations, vibration suppression at rest, and cable unilaterality for all tensegrity structures. Recent works continue to address restricted versions of this problem, indicating it remains open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Tensegrity frameworks: Dynamic analysis review and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: The main issues regarding the control of tensegrity structures are associated to its dynamic model.
status_evidence.claim: The control of tensegrity structures under model uncertainty and disturbances is identified as an open problem.
